key_insight: A small set of retrieved visual examples used to augment textual prompts can substantially close the gap between zero-shot vision–language models and fully supervised segmentation, enabling accurate open‑vocabulary pixel prediction with minimal labelled masks.
problem_solved: Open‑vocabulary segmentation struggles because VLMs are trained with coarse image‑level supervision and natural language prompts are semantically ambiguous for pixel‑level tasks; the paper addresses how to efficiently adapt VLMs to produce accurate masks with only a few example annotations.
method: Few‑shot retrieval: find a small number of visually relevant exemplars (image crops / annotated masks) for each target category to provide concrete visual grounding.
Prompt augmentation & conditioning: fuse retrieved exemplars with text prompts and VLM features to produce stronger, less ambiguous category signals for pixel‑wise prediction.
Lightweight mask adaptation: apply a compact segmentation head or prompt‑conditioning mechanism on top of the VLM to generate high‑quality masks without full supervised re-training.
impact: Enables practitioners to adapt large vision–language models to new segmentation tasks with very few annotations, dramatically reducing labelling cost while achieving performance much closer to fully supervised methods—practical for rapid domain adaptation and long‑tail categories.

paper_title: Retrieve and Segment: Are a Few Examples Enough to Bridge the Supervision Gap in Open-Vocabulary Segmentation?
paper_authors: Tilemachos Aravanis, Vladan Stojnić, Bill Psomas, Nikos Komodakis, Giorgos Tolias
